But did you choose your own life?</div> <div class="choices"> <<button [[Read the creators’ reflection|reflection]]>><</button>> <<button [[Play again and challenge your fate|start]]>><<run setup.resetGame()>><</button>> </div><div class="eyebrow">Passage 20 • Reflection & Bibliography</div> <h2 class="scene-title">Behind the Crossroads</h2> <h3>Group Reflection</h3> <p>We designed this story as a mission-based journey because career decisions rarely happen in a straight line. The three career doors create nonlinear pathways, while shared scenes reconnect the narrative and show that students in different fields still face pressure, rejection, uncertainty, and ethical choices.</p> <p>Early decisions return later: résumé honesty affects the background check, preparation affects the interview, and relationships affect the final test. Career, Integrity, and Wellness scores demonstrate that “success” has several meanings. Humor makes the story inviting, while countdowns, mysterious messages, sound, visual effects, and delayed results create pressure and audience engagement.</p> <p>We avoided presenting one career or family background as universally correct. Instead, outcomes show tradeoffs and encourage players to replay the story from another perspective.</p> <h3>Team Contributions</h3> <p><b>Person 1 — Zhaoyu Wang:</b> Passages 1–6, opening mystery, identity pressure, résumé dilemma, career selection.<br><b>Person 2 — Carlyn Sharp:</b> Passages 7–14, career missions, waiting game, interview, rejection, secret offer.<br><b>Person 3 — Mohammad Ibrahim:</b> Passages 15–20, consequences, final crisis, endings, technical testing, reflection.</p> <h3>Starter Bibliography</h3> <p>Vanderbilt University Career Center. Career exploration and preparation resources.<br>Twine. <i>Twine Reference and Documentation.</i><br>Group-created narrative, dialogue, scoring system, and original ethical dilemmas.</p> <p><i>Replace
